claim: Cao & Han (Journal of Financial Economics, 2013) find delta-hedged equity option returns fall monotonically with the underlying stock's idiosyncratic volatility; a low-minus-high idiosyncratic-volatility strategy earns roughly 1-2% per month at mid quotes but approximately zero after paying 50-100% of the bid-ask spread, and the effect is smaller for large-cap stocks.

evidence.quote: delta-hedged equity option return decreases monotonically with an increase in the idiosyncratic volatility of the underlying stock.
Adding trading friction equal to 50%, 75% or 100% of the closing option bid-ask spread incrementally reduces average profitability from about 1% per month to approximately zero.
The average return decreases systematically with the market capitalization of the underlying stock.

claim: In Cao & Han's 1996-2009 sample, delta-hedged long equity calls lost on average about 4.89% of the option price when held from about 1.5 months before expiry to expiry.

evidence.quote: delta-hedged call options lose on average 4.89% (0.48%) of the option (underlying stock) price from 1.5 months before expiration to expiration.
